title: runmill configuration
description: Operator policy for Runmill, the delivery loop for autonomous software factories. Generated policy files reference a schema stored beside them for editor autocomplete and inline validation.

version.description: Config format version. A binary reading a version it does not understand fails with a named error rather than guessing.

autonomy.description: observe: plan only, no repository mutation. pr-only: implement, verify, review, open a PR, never merge. guarded-merge and continuous are experimental and also require experimental.automatic_merge: true plus a GitHub App token without administration.

automatic_merge.description: Required explicit acknowledgement for the experimental guarded-merge and continuous modes. Selecting an autonomy mode alone never enables automatic merge.

provider.description: Linear is the only live backlog adapter in this preview. Unsupported providers are rejected during configuration validation.

delivered_state.description: Terminal state for pr-only mode, entered at PR_DELIVERED. Distinct from completed_state, which means merged.

allow_unassigned.description: When false, claim_assignee is required and only issues already assigned to that exact id are eligible.

claim_assignee.description: Exact Linear assignee id Runmill may claim as its automation identity.

unprioritized_last.description: Linear encodes no-priority as 0 and urgent as 1, so a naive ascending sort puts unprioritized issues first. When true the sort key maps 0 to positive infinity.

repositories.description: Ordered match rules. First match wins. Every rule must target the same owner/name as the local origin in this single-repository release. No match, or two matches at the same precedence, makes the issue ineligible with a named reason rather than a guess.

branch_template.description: Must contain {attempt}. Without it a retry or post-takeover run reuses the previous run's branch; GitHub rejects the duplicate PR with 422 and runmill would silently adopt the prior run's PR, inheriting its reviews and CI history.

draft_pr.description: Note that many workflows carry `if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false`, so no checks run while draft, and auto-merge cannot be enabled on a draft. Marking ready for review is an explicit transition before CI_WAIT.

merge.description: Merge queue usage is discovered from the branch ruleset and is deliberately not configurable here; a local flag would be a stale mirror of a remote control.

git_isolation.description: clone is required because its self-contained Git metadata can be mounted read-only inside the agent sandbox.

sandbox.description: native resolves to Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap on Linux, chosen by doctor rather than by the user. `none` is rejected unless the run is in observe mode.

network.description: proxy currently enables unrestricted provider egress. Hostname-filtered proxying is planned but not implemented; doctor reports this limitation. none disables provider network access.

network_allowlist.description: Reserved for the planned network proxy. Non-empty values are rejected so an unenforced allowlist cannot be mistaken for policy.

allow_unenforced.description: Reserved for a future per-control acknowledgement flow. Non-empty values are rejected because Runmill does not yet consume this policy.

fail_on_skipped_check.description: When true, every required local check must produce a newly generated, parseable declared report. runmill init sets false for pr-only because the portable starter commands have no framework-specific report declaration; guarded-merge and continuous require true. Observed zero-test, focused, and undeclared-skip results always fail.

report.description: Runmill pre-creates this exact file as the only writable path in otherwise read-only base and candidate verification checkouts; the reporter must overwrite it. JUnit, TAP, and Go JSON are parsed into exact test identities. Missing, stale, malformed, empty, duplicate-id, escaping, and unsupported reports fail the inventory proof.

default.description: Baseline risk tier. Only low-risk runs are eligible for automatic merge; all other tiers require manual approval.

paths.description: Repository-relative paths or *, **, and ? globs. A match in the final diff requires manual approval before merge.

labels.description: Issue labels that require manual approval before merge. Matching is case-insensitive.

conditions.description: Deterministic conditions with local evidence are evaluated. Conditions Runmill cannot prove fail closed instead of being ignored.

daily_cost_usd.description: Durable per-repository spend cap. Requires every configured provider to report dollar cost.

daily_window.description: Calendar boundary used by the durable daily spend ledger.

max_agent_invocations.description: Per-role, not global. A single global cap is exhausted by implementation and local review alone, leaving nothing for PR review.

cost_enforcement.description: auto enforces provider-reported dollar cost and refuses when a configured cap is unknown. wall-and-invocations-only is valid only without max_cost_usd_per_issue or daily_cost_usd. Token-price estimation is not implemented.

providers.description: Which agent runs which role, plus the invocation limits both share.

max_turns.description: Passed to Claude Code for each invocation. Codex CLI has no equivalent turn flag, so Codex is bounded by timeout_minutes and the issue invocation and wall-time budgets instead.

model.description: Model id passed to the CLI. Omit for the CLI's default.

Defaults to the implementer's model when both roles use the same CLI; a different provider uses its own CLI default. A different model on the same CLI is a valid and often the cheapest independent second opinion.
